fullText:
Some of the best overall high school football players are viewed as safety prospects at the next level. The updated 2027 Rivals300 rankings are loaded with exciting two-way playmakers who will likely end up in the secondary next year.

Of Rivals' top 300 prospects in the 2027 cycle, 28 are safeties. As of Sept. 17, all 28 are committed. Eleven of those commitments have landed in the Big Ten. The SEC is next with eight, leaving seven for the ACC, one for the Big 12 and one for the Notre Dame.

Rivals is taking a look at the top 10 safety prospects in the 2027 Rivals300, along with how well their high school programs have performed so far this fall, now that the season is at least a couple weeks old across most of the nation.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 18 NATL.
School: Hampton (Ga.)
Committed Since: Nov. 1, 2025

Dorsey just put together one of the best individual performances you'll ever see from a defensive back. In a win over North Clayton, he picked off four passes and scored a touchdown, leading Hampton to its first win of the season. Last fall, Dorsey had 61 tackles and four INTs while also totaling 13 TDs on the offensive side of the ball. The Hornets are 1-2 entering this week.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 35 NATL.
School: Waxahachie (Texas)
Committed Since: Nov. 16, 2025

Through three games for Waxahachie, Snell has 19 tackles and a pair of pass deflections. He stacked over 140 tackles over his sophomore and junior campaigns. The Indians are currently 3-0 and rank as the No. 25 team in the nation and No. 4 team in Texas, per the Rivals Composite Rankings.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 43 NATL.
School: Millard North (Neb.)
Committed Since: Aug. 15, 2025

In two games, Pittman has tallied nine catches for 282 yards and four touchdowns, 40 rushing yards and one score on the ground, as well as 11 tackles and a pass deflection. Millard North is now 2-1 and ranks as the No. 7 team in Nebraska, per the Rivals Composite Rankings. Across the previous three seasons for Omaha Central, Pittman picked off eight passes and had more than 150 tackles.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 76 NATL.
School: Douglas County (Ga.)
Committed Since: July 18

Normally one of the top HSFB programs in Georgia, Douglas County is off to a 1-2 start and ranks as the No. 36 team in the Peach State. In the first game of the season, Cole had nine tackles and a fumble recovery, according to MaxPreps.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 83 NATL.
School: Broken Arrow (Okla.)
Committed Since: April 23

After a massive win over Owasso, Broken Arrow is now 3-0 and ranks as the No. 2 team in Oklahoma, per the Rivals Composite Rankings. In two games, Stanford has caught six passes and turned them into 131 yards and a touchdown. He's also notched seven tackles.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 85 NATL.
School: Howard (Ga.)
Committed Since: July 17

Howard is 1-2 thus far, but Poole has been the star of the show for the Huskies. He's got two interceptions and seven tackles as a DB. On the offensive side of the ball, he's caught seven passes for 118 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 59 yards and a TD.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 91 NATL.
School: Halls (Tenn.)
Committed Since: May 18

Chandler is the top prospect on Halls, which is 0-4 early on this season. The Clemson commit remains dynamic on both sides of the ball, despite the rough start. In a season-opening loss to Oak Ridge, he had 11 tackles and a sack, per MaxPreps.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 105 NATL.
School: North Miami Beach (Fla.)
Committed Since: June 14

Hyppolite has been excelling on both sides of the ball for a while. Playing quarterback in a win over North Miami last month, he threw for 181 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 69 yards. North Miami Beach is now 3-1 and ranks as the No. 120 team in the Sunshine State, per the Rivals Composite Rankings. Last season, he had 63 tackles, 405 receiving yards and four touchdowns.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 109 NATL.
School: Effingham County (Ga.)

Back in the spring, Albright was expected to transfer to St. Frances, the No. 2 overall team in the Rivals Composite Rankings. Instead, he's back at Effingham County, and according to MaxPreps, he's got 17 tackles, an interception and a rushing touchdown through three games. The Rebels are 1-2 entering this week.

Rivals300 Ranking: No. 117 NATL.
School: Prattville (Ala.)
Committed Since: June 27

Prattville is now 4-0 and checks in at No. 5 in the Alabama Rivals Composite Rankings. Aparicio-Bailey has led the charge on defense, racking up 19 total tackles, two pass deflections, two forced fumbles, one recovery and an interception. He transferred to the Lions from Oak Mountain.

title: Manchester City x Norwich City - Highlights, Summary and Match Report
description: Manchester City produced a commanding performance at the Etihad Stadium, beating Norwich City 5-0 in the third round of the Carabao Cup. With 66% possession and 13 shots to Norwich’s four, the home ...
fullText:
Manchester City began their Carabao Cup title defence in emphatic fashion, cruising past Norwich City 5-0 at the Etihad Stadium.

The main talking point was the outstanding debut of 17-year-old Floyd Samba, who struck twice to announce himself on the first-team stage. The teenager, whose father Chris Samba enjoyed a lengthy Premier League career, headed City ahead after Allan's delivery found him inside the area.

Norwich struggled to contain City's pace and movement, with Rayan Cherki doubling the advantage shortly afterwards following a clever pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The hosts continued to dominate after the interval. Allan turned provider into goalscorer, cutting inside before firing a composed low finish into the corner.

Samba then produced the highlight of the evening, curling a superb effort beyond the Norwich goalkeeper to complete his brace.

Ryan McAidoo completed the scoring in the closing stages after arriving at the far post to finish another flowing City attack.

Norwich briefly appeared to have scored through substitute Mohamed Toure, but the effort was correctly ruled out for offside, leaving City with a comfortable clean sheet.

title: Jürgen Klopp backs Liverpool's Florian Wirtz after Toni Kroos' criticism ahead of Nations League
description: German national team boss Jürgen Klopp has been quick to defend Florian Wirtz after the Liverpool playmaker was the subject of a sarcastic dig from ex-Real Madrid star Toni Kroos
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp has called for the pressure on Florian Wirtz to be eased as he discussed his initial conversations with the Liverpool playmaker following his appointment as Germany head coach.

Wirtz has encountered criticism for his displays at both club and international level since completing a £116 million ($156.3 million) transfer from Bayer Leverkusen to the Reds in summer 2025, with scrutiny in his homeland intensifying after Germany's disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign.

Germany legend Toni Kroos delivered a sarcastic jab at the playmaker on his 'Einfach Mal Luppen' podcast earlier this week - one he hosts with his brother, Felix.

'I managed Wrexham - this is exactly what Rob and Ryan need to do with Phil Parkinson'

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino on dropping Christian Pulisic and selecting 'special' Cavan Sullivan

The duo were asked to identify three players they wanted included in Klopp's inaugural Germany squad who had not represented their nation at the World Cup. And the former Real Madrid midfielder mockingly selected Wirtz as one of his three picks as he targeted the midfielder's World Cup performances, via the Liverpool Echo.

"(Aleksandr) Pavlovic, (Florian) Wirtz, and (Jamal) Musiala," he responded, with his brother apparently initially failing to grasp the joke before interjecting: "What? Which World Cup did you guys miss? Oh, (you say that) because they went unnoticed (and it's as if they weren't there)?"

Wirtz registered three assists at the World Cup and featured in all four of his country's matches as Germany endured a round-of-32 elimination on penalties against Paraguay.

Meanwhile, after recording seven goals and eight assists across 49 appearances during his debut season on Merseyside, he has registered another assist in his five matches so far this campaign.

Fully cognizant of the criticism the midfielder has endured over the past year, Klopp was swift to support Wirtz after naming the 23-year-old in the second of two rosters for Germany's forthcoming four UEFA Nations League matches in the extended September/October international window.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"The communication has been very pleasant," he said. "We keep in touch from time to time. "I think he's the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

"We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.

"When the team works, then every player shines as a consequence. You have to be satisfied with a game in which Flo Wirtz gave everything but didn't have a goal or assist.

"We simply have to give the boy the feeling: 'That was more than good enough today. You helped us as a team. We won 1-0 or 2-0.'

"And then all the experts sit there and discuss why it still didn't work out for him. There are just as many reasons to say: 'He is performing perfectly fine.' Now we'll take the next steps together. That applies for Flo and all the others."

title: Debut delight for Samba and Allan as City power past Norwich
description: Teenager Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream debut, bagging a brilliant brace – with fellow debutant Allan also on target - as City began the defence of the Carabao Cup with a fine 5-0 third-round win at ho...
fullText:
Teenager Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream debut, bagging a brilliant brace – with fellow debutant Allan also on target - as City began the defence of the Carabao Cup with a fine 5-0 third-round win at home to Norwich.

17-year-old Academy graduate Samba was one of a trio afforded their maiden City starts alongside Gerónimo Rulli and Allan.

And he truly enjoyed a night to savour by first opening the scoring with a 29th minute header before then bagging a brilliant second early in the second half.

Allan more than made his mark too, the Brazilian winger marking his Etihad bow with a superb second half effort after Rayan Cherki had also struck before the break.

And an 89th minute effort from substitute Ryan McAidoo rounded off the evening perfectly.

It may have been a different-looking City, with Enzo Maresca making 10 changes in total from Sunday's 1-0 derby win at United, but the end result and dominant display was comfortingly familiar.

City's reward for what was a sixth straight win in all competitions is a fourth-round home tie against Brighton late next month.

With the fixtures coming fast and furious, Blues boss Maresca chose the onset of this season's Carabao Cup to freshen things up.

And debutant Samba – entrusted with the central striking role with Erling Haaland rested – was straight into the action, superbly teeing up Rico Lewis for a ninth minute shot that was a fraction over.

With Norwich packing bodies behind the ball and seeking to break on the counter it required patience and composure for City

But our approach was rewarded on 29 minutes with a dream debut goal for Samba.

Nico O'Reilly fired in a deep cross from the left flank which was diverted to Allan on the oppositive wing.

The Brazilian did well to instantly despatch an inviting ball into the heart of the box and Samba showed brilliant awareness and poise to steer a deft header home to the delight of the Etihad.

Within three minutes City's grip on the game was further solidified as Cherki doubled the advantage.

Ayyoub Bouaddi was the provider, the Moroccan threading a neat pass from the middle of the Blues' half that was diverted into the path of the onrushing Cherki.

The French wizard needed no second invitation to power on before drilling a low shot past former City keeper Daniel Grimshaw.

It almost got better for City and Samba on 39 minutes as the teenager burst clear again in the Canaries box before a timely block from Kellen Fisher averted the danger.

However just three minutes after the restart a third goal did arrive – as Allan marked his City debut in memorable fashion too – the winger cutting in from the left of the box before firing home a low shot past Grimshaw.

And the Samba beat then continued on 54 minutes.

Rayan Aït-Nouri fed Samba on the right of the box and the teenager coolly curled a brilliant shot past Grimshaw.

Norwich did have the ball in the City net via Mohamed Toure on 75 minutes but the Canaries sub was flagged for offside as Rulli enjoyed a clean sheet on his bow

And a perfect night was then rounded off a minute into injury time when substitute Ryan McAidoo found the target, his sweet finish rounding off a flowing move.

CITY XI: Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić, Samba, Allan (Braithwaite 71), Aït-Nouri, Cherki (McAidoo 45)

Subs: Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo.

NORWICH: Grimshaw, Fisher, Alves (McConville 71), Darling, Yongwa, Wright, Field, Crnac (Musaba 62), Slimane (Toure 71), Diallo (Maghoma 45), Kvistgaarden (Schwartau 85)

Subs: Kovacevic, Stacey, Chrisene, Mattsson.

The 17-year-old was afforded the responsibility of leading the line and thrived in the role.

Aside from his two superb strikes, he was a real handful for the visitors every time he got on the ball and looked totally at home on the big stage.

It was yet more compelling evidence of the amazing production line of talent that constantly emerges from City's famed Academy.

And for Samba it's a night he will never, ever forget!

Tonight's victory also extended City's fine home record against the Canaries.

It means City have now won seven of our last eight home games against Norwich City in all competitions (L1).

What's more, City have now our last five games in a row by an aggregate score of 23-1.

City's reward for tonight's victory is a fourth-round tie at home to Brighton and Hove Albion.

The tie is set to be played at the Etihad in the week beginning October 26 with a precise date and kick-off time to be confirmed in due course.

The Blues' final fixture ahead of the September international break is back here at the Etihad when we play host to Sunderland in the Premier League.

Kick-off for what is another crucial clash is set for 14.00 (UK).

title: Gallery: Samba and Allan soar against Canaries!
description: Floyd Samba netted a brace, whilst fellow debutant Allan scored one and assisted another, as we progressed into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a 5-0 victory over Norwich. Match Report Debut ...
fullText:
Floyd Samba netted a brace, whilst fellow debutant Allan scored one and assisted another, as we progressed into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a 5-0 victory over Norwich.

Enzo Maresca handed debuts to summer-signings Allan and Gerónimo Rulli, as well as 17-year-old Samba, and it was two of the debutants who combined to put us ahead just after the half-hour mark.

Nico O'Reilly's deep cross found Allan at the back post and the winger picked out Samba, who expertly headed into the bottom left corner.

Three minutes later, we doubled the lead with Samba influential again, knocking the ball into Ayyoub Bouaddi's path.

The Moroccan midfielder slid Rayan Cherki through on goal and he did the rest, coolly slotting into the corner.

Allan switched to the left flank after the interval and the move paid off immediately, as he jinxed in and out before driving into the far corner for his first goal for the Club.

Six minutes shy of the hour mark, Samba was the centre of attention again, receiving the ball from Rayan Aït-Nouri before curling into the bottom right corner superbly for his second of the evening.

Ryan McAidoo added a late fifth to put the icing on the cake as we deservedly booked a place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup, where we will host Brighton and Hove Albion.

title: Joe Burrow Thinks It’s ‘Ridiculous’ to Sit Out Next Game Despite Back Concerns
description: The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback is dealing with back tightness following the team’s Week 1 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
fullText:
Joe Burrow dismissed the idea of sitting out the next game despite dealing with ongoing back soreness

The Bengals quarterback has a history of playing through injuries, including a strained calf and appendicitis

"If I'm not getting surgery, I'll be out there," Burrow said

The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback, 29, dismissed the idea of sitting out the next game, despite dealing with back tightness after the team's season-opening win against the Buccaneers.

Burrow, who was limited in practice on Wednesday, Sept. 16, was then asked by a reporter in a post-practice press conference if he would rest.

"Is there any part of you that doesn't want to play on Sunday out of precaution?" the reporter asked.

Without hesitation, Burrow responded, "No."

"That's ridiculous," the QB continued. "I think every game is so important to me. I'm going to do what it takes to be out there."

He then quipped: "If I'm not getting surgery, I'll be out there."

Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Bengals' 33-27 Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

The Bengals quarterback said he started to feel soreness in the hours following the game; however, he isn't exactly sure when he sustained the injury, per ESPN. While he was sacked just once, he took a significant hit while scrambling for a first down. The play kept the drive alive and ultimately led to a touchdown pass.

When looking back on his decision, Burrow was content with the result.

"I was comfortable with it," he said. "It was either that or kick a field goal. It's a decision that I made."

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — 

The two-time MVP finalist has dealt with several injuries throughout his seven-year career.

Last season, Burrow suffered a severe turf toe injury in Week 2. After undergoing surgery and taking nine games to recover, he returned to action in late November and started the final six games of the season. It was the third time he had been placed on injured reserve.

Burrow is no stranger to playing through injuries.

In 2022, the Bengals QB didn't miss any games despite undergoing an emergency appendectomy at the beginning of training camp that left him briefly hospitalized. The next year, he didn't skip any snaps despite dealing with a strained calf in preseason that he aggravated in Week 2.

title: Bold predictions for Bills vs. Lions TNF Week 2
description: Three bold performances that could lift the Buffalo Bills to victory against the Detroit Lions in Week 2
fullText:
After waiting months to see what the newest version of the Buffalo Bills would look like in action, fans have been treated to two regular-season games in the span of five days. With the Bills hosting the Detroit Lions for the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium in primetime for Thursday Night Football on Prime, there hasn't been a ton of time to reflect on their game in Week 1.

So, what can we take away from Buffalo's thrilling victory over the Houston Texans last Sunday? It's clear the offense is going to attack opponents, and it's also likely that quarterback Josh Allen will need to orchestrate a large handful of points each game. That is, at least unless the running game finds easier sledding and the defense begins to click to the point that games don't always feel like it's a last-team-with-the-ball-wins situation.

Allen was incredible in Houston, and so was tight end Dalton Kincaid, and wide receivers DJ Moore. With a couple of real game-changing plays to claim strip sacks of quarterback C.J. Stroud, outside linebacker Greg Rousseau had one of the finest performances of his career.

If you're curious how I did in Week 1, take a look. What's in store for Thursday Night Football? Here are a few bold predictions…

Okay, maybe this isn't such a bold prediction. But it's not a given when you consider who's on the Lions' roster. The last time these teams squared off, quarterback Jared Goff led the way with the most total yards — going 38-of-59 for 494 yards and five touchdowns, plus two carries for 13 yards. Allen finished that game 23-of-34 for 362 yards and two touchdowns, adding 11 carries for 68 yards and two rushing scores.

Given the state of each team's defensive roster for Week 2, I expect a shootout. This time, Allen shouldn't have to rely on the underneath stuff so much, and I expect him to flirt or surpass the 400-yard mark. Detroit has some real concerns at safety with both starters there out of the lineup. In Week 1, quarterback Tyler Shough hit the Lions with a final statline of 35-of-56 for 410 yards, with three touchdowns and two interceptions.

Allen is on a completely different level than Shough, and he often plays his best football in primetime. FanDuel Sportsbook currently has Josh Allen at +265 to throw for 300+ yards. With Allen in Week 2, you can wager all the way up to 375+ yards, which has him with +1200 odds.

This is all before considering what Allen brings to the table as a rusher. If you're looking to really dive into the odds, Allen's least-likely rushing yards wager in this game is at 40+ yards (+158). If, like in Week 1, the defense sets out to limit running back James Cook III, it's possible Allen finds his way to the type of yardage he piled up the last time these teams met. It's unlikely he leads the game in rushing, and that's reflected in his +1900 yards to do it.

If anyone's capable of pulling it all off in primetime, it's Josh Allen.

In Week 1 Dalton Kincaid was unstoppable, a true matchup nightmare and a highly potent X-factor against Houston's vaunted defense. Kincaid finished with five catches (6 targets) for 130 yards. Head coach Joe Brady called a game that asked Kincaid to play featured snaps way down the middle of the field, and also outside as a boundary receiver.

Kincaid is a tight end by trade, but he profiles like wide receiver with true size and speed. He's very important to what the Bills intend to do in 2026, which is utilizing a heavy dose of 13 personnel.

Right now, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Kincaid with the fourth-best odds (+650) to finish Thursday night's game with the most receiving yards. It's not a guarantee, simply because we don't have weeks of data to back up Kincaid's potential as one of the NFL's elite yardage receivers. Now the healthiest he's been in several seasons, Kincaid may be ready for a truly breakout season.

Add in the aforementioned injury woes for Detroit's starting safety tandem, and I believe Brady will look to test the defense with Kincaid the mismatch king. Interestingly, FanDuel lists Kincaid with only +230 odds to record a 30+ yard reception.

Add it all up, and that should mean another 100-plus yard receiving day and maybe the first touchdown of the season for Kincaid.

As discussed in this article's intro, Rousseau was absolutely dynamite last Sunday. Claiming a strip-sack of Stroud on Houston's opening drive of the game, and repeating the effort on the Texans' last drive of regulation served as major turning points. It's possible that without those two plays by Rousseau, the Bills struggle to win in Houston.

This will be just Rousseau's second game at outside linebacker — ever in his NFL career. Yes, there's now film on his work at the position, but Rousseau carries X-factor potential as a very large human being at outside linebacker.

FanDuel currently lists Rousseau with the second-best odds of recording a sack (-108), and I like him to push for a second. Rousseau hadn't played this explosive ever in prior head coach Sean McDermott's scheme. Now off the line a bit, his length and speed can be put to much better use. He might even find his way to another turnover or pass breakup.

The Lions' injury woes have also decimated their starting offensive line. Bet on Groot to dominate Detroit Thursday night.

Think you've got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now to put it to the test!

title: Oregon vs. Portland State position-by-position: Who has the edge?
description: Breaking down the positional edges, stats and more between the No. 21 Oregon Ducks and Portland State in Week 3.
fullText:
That's the story of the week for the Oregon Ducks. Coming off an ugly and brutal loss to a beleaguered Oklahoma State, the Ducks return home focused on righting wrongs and getting back on the track toward a national championship.

The path is crowded with more obstacles, but it starts this week against winless Portland State. The Vikings are outmatched and outgunned against the Ducks, but Oregon is in no position to take an opponent for granted. The Ducks have issues to sort out on both sides of the ball, and while the team isn't looking ahead anymore, the goal is to build confidence and see the team execute before heading to USC next week.

Like a basketball player in a slump, sometimes it's best to get a couple of easy shots just to see the ball go through the basket, building some confidence. That's exactly what Oregon is aiming to do this week against the Vikings, and the offense should be able to hit on several big shots against Portland State's lowly defense.

Oregon is a 58.5-point favorite, the largest point spread for the Ducks under Dan Lanning, and for good reason. If all of the pieces come together, as many expect they should, the Ducks could put this game to rest quickly. Let's dive into the numbers with each team's projected starters and take a look at the "Tale of the Tape" for the matchup. We will see if we can get a sense of how this game will play out on Friday night.

Gabe Downing has turned Portland State into a passing offense, so he won't be worn down if he has to throw the ball 50 times against Oregon. Although Dante Moore had his worst showing with the Ducks last weekend, this is a spot where he can get right and build some momentum moving into conference play. It would be nice to see Moore use his legs to extend plays more, but above all else, he needs to establish a rhythm with his receivers in this game. I'll take Moore having a big bounce-back outing.

Neither Oregon nor Portland State has had an explosive rushing game this season. Jordon Davison didn't finish the game last week, and Dierre Hill Jr. had a critical fumble. Neither of them has surpassed 100 yards in a game yet, and the rushing attack has been silent because of a lack of push from the offensive line and a lack of creativity in the play calling. Fortunately for the Ducks, the Vikings haven't been able to stop the run this season, allowing over 200 yards in each of the last two games, so this is another chance for the Ducks to get back on track. Delon Thompson is the bellcow back for the Vikings, totalling over 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns the last two seasons, but he has been off to a slow start this season.

It was a tough week for the Oregon pass catchers, who dropped several passes from Moore in the loss to Oklahoma State. Still, the Ducks are no match for the Vikings here and should be able to produce several explosive plays to boost their numbers moving forward. The Vikings have a couple of threats, including wideout Terence Loville, who leads the team with 221 yards, and tight end Tanner Beaman, who has 157 yards. Both the Ducks and Vikings could be missing key weapons, like Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson, who is questionable to play with an injury, and Portland State wideout Devon Anderson, who had a great debut but didn't play last week.

On the ground and through the air, the Ducks' defense was ripped apart last week. However, Portland State just allowed over 600 yards of offense to North Dakota, so I'll take the Oregon front seven creating some pressure and the secondary forcing turnovers against a pass-heavy offense from the Vikings. The Ducks had their first two interceptions a week ago, including a pick-six, so despite the big plays the unit suffered, Oregon's defense should be able to force similar mistakes and play a more complete game this week.

Obviously, Oregon has a significant edge over the winless FCS program. I'd like to think the Ducks come into this game with a little extra fire and a desire to leave no doubt, but it does need to be proven on the field that they are capable of that, and so far this season, they have not. Oregon should be able to run or pass at will against a Portland State defense that hasn't stopped anyone this season, but I would really like to see the Ducks get after Downing in the pocket and force turnovers in the secondary.

It's odd to say that in a game between a preseason national championship favorite and an FCS team, it's Oregon that has a lot to prove. But the point is valid. The Ducks were exposed last week, and this is their only chance to patch some holes and restore any confidence before tackling another big test next week at USC.

I'll take Oregon to win big and comfortably, and as I have said in each "Tale of the Tape" so far, I think some of the backups will finally get a shot. Portland State's offense has some weapons capable of making big plays, but the Ducks have the talent and need to shut down any hope the Vikings could have coming into Autzen Stadium.

title: Reds roster move coming? Tyler Stephenson exits but avoids injury?
description: The Chase Burns Workload Limit plan needs a tweak after piggyback partner Brandon Williamson was unexpectedly needed in Reds' loss to Dodgers.
fullText:
An otherwise sleepy-looking loss to the World Series champs Thursday (Sept. 17) could have ramifications for the Cincinnati Reds roster, possibly a key pitcher and maybe even a veteran catcher.

When Reds starter Brady Singer struggled enough early enough in an 8-2 loss to the Dodgers, it made for extra work for a recently taxed bullpen, which meant pulling the Brandon Williamson lever a day early. The lefty pitched two innings of relief.

Reds Dodgers Elly De La Cruz Is Elly De La Cruz performing like he's applying for job with Dodgers?

Reds Dodgers Elly De La Cruz Elly De La Cruz homers again as Cincinnati Reds halt skid vs. Dodgers

That probably means a roster move before this weekend's series opener against the Chicago Cubs, because Chase Burns is the Friday scheduled starter, and Williamson — Burns' piggyback partner under a strict workload-limit plan — is out for that game.

Burns has been limited to three innings per start his last two starts, with Williamson picking up the bulk after that in each start.

Reds manager Terry Francona said team officials were working postgame on other options for the backside of the Burns start against the Cubs.

"We've got some things to work through, obviously," Francona said.

As for the veteran catcher, Tyler Stephenson was forced to stop the game for a painful cramp in his upper left leg. After a few minutes of stretching and swallowing a quick shot of "pickle juice" hydration provided by the trainer, he stayed in the game.

But when he drove a ball to the wall in right-center for an apparent double, he was only able to hobble to first base, at that point exiting for a pinch-runner.

"We gave him the old pickle juice, but it didn't quite (take care of it)," Francona said. "It's a pretty hot day, especially for September. He was having trouble, you could tell."

Francona said the issue didn't appear to worsen beyond a cramp.

title: What Browns defenders said was reason for dismal debut against Jaguars
description: Mike Rutenberg made his defensive coordinator debut in the Browns' opener. His players know what went wrong, but now it's about fixing the problems.
fullText:
BEREA ― The cause of the problem is, honestly, quite simple. So, too, is the solution.

The Browns defense has identified those from the season-opening loss at the Jacksonville Jaguars. It turned out it was one and the same: Execution.

"Yeah, definitely just playing 11 as one," defensive end Jared Verse said Sept. 17. "The scheme is set perfectly. The coverages are set perfectly for us not to get aerated. Upfront is set perfectly for us not to be knocked back and to leave gaps open. So if we just do our job, our one of 11, we're going to be good when we're done."

The fact the offense struggled in the opener with Deshaun Watson at quarterback wasn't a stunning development. There were a multitude of factors which gave everyone reason to believe that could've happened.

The defense, though, was seen as a strength. Even with a change at defensive coordinator from Jim Schwartz to Mike Rutenberg and a change at defensive end from Myles Garrett to Verse, there were plenty of reasons to believe that side of the ball would still be able to hold its own against the Jaguars.

That is, until Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence went out and, in Verse's words, "aerated" them. He completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns, rarely feeling the heat from the Browns' pass rush.

"I think looking at it, obviously that's not what we wanted as the outcome and wanted to put on tape," linebacker Carson Schwesinger said. "And so it's a matter of just looking at it and seeing where we went wrong. And I think a lot of it comes down to just the execution of it. I think you can see us playing hard out there. It's being able to execute what we do all week."

Before the Browns could move on to the next challenge, another Florida road trip, this time to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, they had to diagnose the problem. Was it the matter of a simple tune-up, or was there a much more systematic issue that was at the root of the problem?

Jacksonville scored on six of their first seven possessions, leading 24-0 at halftime, 31-0 one drive into the third quarter and 34-3 after three quarters. The Jaguars averaged 6.4 yards per play on 56 plays, including 10.6 yards per attempt on every pass.

Rutenberg's scheme has come under scrutiny because multiple players have said more zone was run than it had been previously under Schwartz. The Browns played the highest amount of man coverage in the league in 2025.

"This is one game of the season, so I wouldn't just throw everything away or just feel like it's the end of the world after one game," cornerback Denzel Ward said. "We got to execute and do things in zone or do things in whatever the play call may be and execute and do our job. I think that's the biggest thing, us doing our job. But, yeah, I don't think it's the end of the world. I don't think that we're not capable of playing zone or we can only play one thing, but we just got to do our job. That's the biggest thing."

Schwesinger may have summed it up even more succinctly. The 2025 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year was asked about how there's been so much talk about man versus zone, but cut off the question with a simple, "That's not the reason."

The way the Browns defense worked when it was among the best in the NFL was that the pass rush up front would lead to a rushed quarterback. That rushed quarterback, assuming he got away from the defensive linemen, would either throw off-target or into coverage, which is where the Browns were able to get turnovers.

The Browns, according to Pro Football Focus, only managed 10 total pressures against Jacksonville, including the lone sack by defensive tackle Mason Graham. PFF also had Lawrence under pressure on six drop-backs, and he still completed 2-of-4 passes, and both went for touchdowns.

"It's all facets of the game where we want to continue to get better," Rutenberg said. "It's not just one thing, it's not just pressure. Collectively, we want to make everything better and that's been our focus this week and we're off to a really good start. It's always going to be collective. We didn't coach it well enough. We didn't coach it to our standard.

"I know the guys hope that they play better and play above the line and that's going to be our focus this entire week. It's that every week. No matter a great game or a poor game, you always want to do it better getting ready for the next week."

title: Red Sox Make Notable Lineup Change For Crucial Rangers Finale
description: The Red Sox are bringing Jarren Duran back into the starting lineup Thursday as Boston tries to avoid a sweep and protect its playoff position against the Rangers.
fullText:
Red Sox Make Notable Lineup Change For Crucial Rangers Finale originally appeared on NESN. 

The Boston Red Sox need something to change Thursday night. Putting Jarren Duran back in the lineup is a start.

Boston will turn to Duran in center field for Thursday's series finale against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field after he did not start Wednesday's 7-3 loss. The Red Sox have dropped the first two games of the series and enter Thursday at 82-70 with only 10 games remaining in the regular season.

Roman Anthony will remain in the leadoff spot and start in left field, while Jahmai Jones gets another opportunity at designated hitter. Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Adley Rutschman make up the middle of the order.

Christopher Smith of MassLive shared Boston's lineup shortly after it was released Thursday.

https://x.com/SmittyOnMLB/status/2100681896715796689

Sonny Gray will start on the mound.

Duran's return is one of the most notable changes from Wednesday's lineup. The 30-year-old was not in the starting nine Wednesday, when Boston used Nate Eaton in center field and Isiah Kiner-Falefa at second base.

Red Sox lineup: Anthony LF, Jones DH, Abreu RF, Contreras 1B, Rutschman C, Story SS, Duran LF, Durbin 3B, Sogard 2B, Gray P

Instead, Duran returns to center, Sogard takes over at second and Trevor Story moves up one spot in the order to hit sixth.

Boston could certainly use a spark.

The Red Sox entered Texas with an opportunity to strengthen their postseason position but instead have lost consecutive games to a Rangers team fighting for its own playoff life. Texas improved to 76-76 with Wednesday's victory and has won four consecutive games. The Rangers are only one game behind the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot.

Boston remains in much better shape, holding the second AL wild card with a five-game cushion over Chicago entering Thursday. That cushion is significant. It isn't comfortable enough to keep losing.

The Red Sox have gone 5-5 over their last 10 games, and Thursday represents their final opportunity to leave Texas with something positive before the schedule moves into its final nine games.

MORE: Red Sox Magic Number for 2026 Playoffs: Tracking Boston's Path to Postseason

If there is a pitcher Boston would want on the mound in this situation, Gray makes a compelling case. The veteran right-hander enters Thursday with a 17-5 record and 2.76 ERA.

Texas will counter with left-hander Tyler Alexander, who enters at 5-2 with a 3.38 ERA. The left-handed starter helps explain some of Boston's lineup decisions.

Jones, a right-handed hitter, remains in the No. 2 spot after starting there Wednesday. Contreras gives Boston another right-handed bat in the cleanup position, while Rutschman follows him from the fifth spot.

Anthony remains atop everything.

Boston has continued trusting the rookie in the leadoff role during the most important stretch of the season, and that won't change with a left-hander on the mound Thursday.

The larger question is whether the Red Sox can finally turn opportunities into enough runs.

Boston's postseason position remains favorable, but the Rangers have provided a reminder of how quickly September can become uncomfortable.

A sweep would send the Red Sox into the final nine games on a three-game losing streak. A win would allow them to leave Texas with their playoff cushion intact and Gray having stopped the bleeding. With Duran back in the lineup, Boston is hoping Thursday looks considerably different from the first two nights of the series. First pitch from Globe Life Field is scheduled for 8:05 p.m. ET.

title: Why Ohio State landed Deng Ngor before Duke, Florida could host visits
description: Ohio State landed a commitment from a top-20 forward when Deng Ngor picked the Buckeyes. Here's how they beat out Duke, Florida and others for him.
fullText:
On a different timeline, Deng Ngor and his family would have been on a plane headed west. For the weekend of Sept. 18, the four-star forward in the class of 2027 was scheduled to be on an official visit to Washington, one of three remaining such trips on his calendar.

After the Huskies, official visits Florida and Duke loomed for Ngor, a fast-rising prospect who added a host of high-major scholarship offers during the late spring and summer. There was just one problem, however: he'd already taken an official visit to Ohio State during the weekend of Sept. 4.

It was Ngor's first visit, and it proved to be the only one he needed. On Sept. 17, the 6-foot-8, 200-pound Canadian forward from Fort Erie (Ontario) International Academy publicly announced his commitment to the Buckeyes, passing on chances to check out his other three finalists.

"We were supposed to visit other big schools like Duke, but for our family it really felt right," said Joseph Ngor, Deng's father. "Security, academic support, small city, the community, the way we were treated there, there was nothing hidden from us, really."

Leading into the Ohio State visit, Joseph Ngor said the family had been doing research on the program to better understand what the situation might be like once they got there. Included in that work was the continual relationship-building between the Ngors and the Ohio State coaching staff since the Buckeyes offered him a scholarship May 28. The Huskies, Gators and Blue Devils would all eventually follow suit, but Ohio State assistant coach Luke Simons quickly established a bond with the family that steadily grew leading into the visit.

All of that came together on the official visit, Joseph Ngor said.

"The coaches, we dined with their families," he said. "As parents, that's what we were looking for, and my kid thinks his career will really excel where he's free. (Ohio State) gave him everything. He's the main guy (they're recruiting) at his position and everything seemed right, so instead of looking for other things we just said no and closed everything up.

"Luke is really great at connecting to the families. He's made a relationship far more than basketball."

When Ngor landed his Ohio State offer, he was unranked in the 247Sports.com database. After a strong spring and summer playing both AAU basketball and for Canada's U18 team, he has climbed to No. 55 in the class of 2027 according to the website. Rivals.com, in its most recent rankings refresh, moved him up to No. 19 nationally.

According to Neilball.com, Deng Ngor has played in 44 games between his high school and the AAU circuit in the past year and averaged 9.9 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game while shooting 52.8% from the field and 30.2% from 3-point range. During the spring and summer, he shot 34% from 3-point range while playing on the adidas circuit.

Ohio State Buckeyes: Value of joy instilled in Ohio State basketball's Amare Bynum from a young age

While helping Canada win a gold medal at the FIBA U18 AmeriCup, Deng Ngor averaged 10.2 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists while shooting 37.5% (6 for 16) from 3-point range.

At Ohio State, Joseph Ngor said the coaches view him as a likely replacement for five-star freshman forward Anthony Thompson, who is widely projected as a first-round NBA draft prospect.

"He's a wing and a free shooter," he said. "The guy that's playing there now is projected to go to the NBA. That's what Jake (Diebler) was telling me, and so they said that he's the main guy for (them). His style of play fits their program, so they're going to adjust some things but he's going to play his style because that's (also) Ohio State's style."

Once the returned home from their Ohio State visit, Joseph Ngor said it felt like just a matter of time before they would commit to the Buckeyes.

"From the first day we visited, we left on (Sept. 6) and we were positive that is the one we were looking for," Joseph Ngor said. "We were talking to those (other) coaches who really wanted us to consider them. We were telling them positive things about our visit and they were saying, 'You're going to see that when you get to our campus. It's going to be pretty much the same, if not better.'

"I had some mixed feelings like, maybe we should just visit all of these schools and pick one later. Then the other part of me said if you do that, you're going to get more confused."

title: Columbus Blue Jackets open camp with Kirill Marchenko's future hazy
description: Kirill Marchenko has vowed to play hard for the Columbus Blue Jackets, but the star forward remains noncommittal about his long-term future.
fullText:
Kirill Marchenko's return for training camp gave Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell and coach Rick Bowness a chance to talk with the right wing about summer reports that he's leaning toward not staying long-term.

More: Kirill Marchenko is back with Columbus Blue Jackets, but for how long?

Waddell met with him twice, but left each time with only an assurance that Marchenko will give a strong effort while he's with the Blue Jackets. Talk about the future remains vague.

"I've sat down with him twice, and the last time for 45 minutes," Waddell said. "Unbelievable conversation with him. His wife's due [to have their first child] the first week of December, I believe it is. We talked about his family and all that."

Waddell's words didn't match up with his demeanor or tone while speaking at the Jackets' media luncheon Sept. 16 at Nationwide Arena. The longtime GM almost choked up while talking about his interactions with Marchenko, who has either led or co-led the team in goals the past three seasons while endearing himself to fans and teammates with a jovial personality.

"Marchy's a good person," Waddell said. "Marchy's thing is ... he's not sure what's going to happen. He'll be [a restricted free agent] again next year. He's got a contract this year. He said, 'Don, I'm going to play my butt off here and help us win.' He's a really good person that cares, so I see no reason why that's going to change."

That sounds hopeful, but Marchenko's desire to stay in Columbus is still hazy at best.

His agent, Dan Milstein, hasn't returned requests from The Dispatch to discuss Marchenko's situation, but an ESPN report during the first day of the draft in late June cited "someone from Marchenko's camp," as saying the star right wing didn't see himself signing a long-term deal with the Blue Jackets.

No specifics were given about the reason for that outlook, and Marchenko quickly became the focus of trade speculation for more than two months. Waddell said he's still getting phone calls from opposing GMs, but none thus far is willing to meet the high price it would take for the Blue Jackets to deal away their top scorer in the final year of a team-friendly contract.

Marchenko had a personal obligation that kept him from speaking with reporters Sept. 17, but he's expected to take questions Sept. 18. Thus far, neither Bowness nor his teammates sense any team chemistry issues with Marchenko this season.

"We watched him the week before camp, every day," Bowness said. "We always made sure that one of us [coaches] was talking to him every day, and I had a great 1-on-1 with him [Sept. 16]. He's here, and he's ready to go. He's a highly-skilled guy. I'm not worried about him. Let's put it that way. He's here, he's committed and we'll get everything we can out of him."

Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com

title: Five stars to watch in the Women’s Champions League this season
description: Europe’s top players are about to put on a show.
fullText:
A new season of the Women's Champions League begins next week with the start of the league phase, and the best players in Europe will once again showcase their brilliance as they look to lead their teams to continental glory.

Here are five players to watch in the new UWCL season.

The three-time Ballon d'Or winner and Barcelona superstar missed almost all of last season with a broken ankle and has made it her goal to return to her best form and lead Barça to a fifth Champions League title.

Barça went through a lot of change this summer and lost club icon Alexia Putellas, who was one of the key pieces in last season's UWCL run and helped make up for Aitana's absence. Now it's time for Bonmatí to restore her status as the world's best player, plus she will be hungry to show her best version in Europe.

When fully healthy, there is no more complete midfielder in the game than Aitana. She can win duels, make key passes, score goals and has a special flair that makes her truly must-see TV.

Even though Aitana is the superstar and the team's best player, there is a serious case to be made for Pina as the most important piece of Barça's new-look squad as they try to continue their dominance in Europe.

Pina has been carefully brought up over the last couple of years and has played primarily as a forward, but the departure of Putellas allowed Barça to unleash Pina in her best position as an attacking midfielder who can create for others and score goals herself.

The 25-year-old is entering her prime and has all the tools to become a superstar, and this Champions League campaign could vault her into the Ballon d'Or conversation next year if she can match the big expectations placed on her shoulders. The talent is certainly there.

The Spanish international made a high-profile switch from Barcelona to Lyon in the summer in what was a real coup for last season's runner-ups, who hope Salma is the missing piece in their quest to dethrone Barça.

Paralluelo is an incredible athlete who combines speed and power and has become one of the best finishers in the game. At the age of 22 and with the responsibility to be Lyon's top forward in the Champions League as they make a title push, Salma is one of the favorites to lead the scoring charts this season.

Another contender to be top scorer this season is Arsenal's Alessia Russo, who scored nine goals last season and is still one of the best forwards in the game. She is part of an Arsenal team that won the title in 2025 and is among the contenders once again. Not to mention, she is a great finisher in front of goal.

Russo plays for a very complete Arsenal side who play strong defense and have a great midfield, but she is responsible for finishing the great team moves with a goal and can always be trusted to deliver when it matters most.

We won't be able to watch the career of one of the best players in the history of the women's game for much longer, so any chance to appreciate the brilliance of Pernille Harder must be appreciated.

Bayern is not currently at the very top of the list of favorites but always deserves respect. Harder is the biggest reason why Bayern gets that respect. She's as complete a forward as the game's ever seen with the ability to lead both the goals and assists charts, and even at the age of 33 she's still one of the best players in Europe at her position.

title: Would a win over Giants really fix the Rams?
description: There are serious questions surrounding Rams’ status as a ‘super team’. Beating the Giants may not bring answers.
fullText:
Who are the 2026 Los Angeles Rams? Apparently not who we thought.

LA was considered a "super team" and a historical Super Bowl favorite entering the year. They were blown out by the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Next to nothing went right for the Rams.

The team's second game—against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football—is unlikely to bring many answers outside of potential confirmation that the Rams are on a downswing. A win would be positive but not overly noteworthy. A loss would send shockwaves across the NFL.

Los Angeles opened as 8.5-point favorites over the Giants. The line is now closer to 7.5.

In short, this is a game the Rams are expected to win. Victory doesn't mean everything is OK and the team is back on track, although it would certainly be encouraging.

The three games that follow New York will be more informative in terms of how the Rams stack up against other contenders:

The Australia trip didn't go as well as you wanted. It's over.

Beat the Giants. Show us your true colors against the Broncos, Eagles, and Bills. Then we can talk.

In the meantime, these are the looming questions that we should track closely:

Will Matthew Stafford bounce back, or are there long-term concerns?

Only Bo Nix and Deshaun Watson were worse in Week 1. Can we chalk up Stafford's bad game to a long Australia trip, or could the end of his career be approaching?

How will the defense fare without Myles Garrett?

I'd expect Desjuan Johnson to play on run downs. Josaiah Stewart will see a lot of run as a pass rusher and coverage changeup. Can LA get by for at least the next four weeks?

What difference will Aaron Donald make, assuming he plays?

If Donald participates against the Giants, will he look like his old self? Will a rising tide lift all boats across the defensive line?

Can Rams get their money's worth out of Jaylen Watson?

Allowed two touchdowns in his first game as a Ram according to some outlets. He was brought in to limit bigger receiving targets and Mike Evans had his way against the defense.

Are special teams really that much better?

Deebo Samuel ripped off long returns in Australia. Special teams has cost Rams several games in recent seasons. Can they avoid disaster or will it be more of the same?

Did the Rams err by doubling down on 13 personnel?

LA's passing game is less effective with three receivers. It's also difficult to come from behind with heavier personnel on the field. Will we look back and say the Rams should have invested more in a third receiver over the offseason?

title: Official: Manchester United confirm three players have signed new deals
description: 1 Manchester United have announced that the talented trio of Fred Heath, Dante Plunkett and Will Murdock have signed brand-new deals.StatementAn official club statement reads, “Goalkeeper Fred Heath...
fullText:
Manchester United have announced that the talented trio of Fred Heath, Dante Plunkett and Will Murdock have signed brand-new deals.

An official club statement reads, "Goalkeeper Fred Heath and defender Dante Plunkett have put pen-to-paper on their first professional deals, while keeper Will Murdock has signed his second professional contract with the club."

"Congratulations to Fred, Will and Dante and we look forward to continuing to track your progress."

Heath, Plunkett and Murdock will be hoping to emulate the talents of previous generations in making the exciting transition from the academy to the first team.

Plunkett has featured 12 times for the Under-18s after arriving from Premier League rivals Aston Villa. He has struggled slightly with injuries.

Meanwhile, Murdock has made the jump to the Under-21s and was part of the United contingent that made its way to the United States for pre-season during the summer of 2025.

The goalkeeper has been a regular for the Red Devils in Premier League 2 and played in the play-off final against Brighton & Hove Albion last term.

Heath has also enjoyed a gradual rise through the youth ranks.

Recent reports that JJ Gabriel has asked to leave immediately have shaken United's academy, though there remains cause for optimism.

This is primarily because of claims that attacking wonderkid Noah Ajayi is on the verge of signing a long-term contract.

It's believed that Ajayi attracted interest from clubs in England and around Europe, but he will commit his long-term future to United.

Ajayi has wasted no time this season, scoring once in his only Under-18s Premier League appearance and he followed that up by featuring against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League last week.

title: Manchester City 5 Norwich City 0: Thoughts and observations from City’s routine victory
description: Manchester City 5 (Floyd Samba 29′, 54′, Rayan Cherki 32′, Allan 48′, Ryan McAidoo 90′)Norwich City 0Tonight has seen Manchester City begin their Carabao Cup defence in style with a 5-0 win ...
fullText:
Tonight has seen Manchester City begin their Carabao Cup defence in style with a 5-0 win over Norwich City at the Etihad Stadium. A brace from Floyd Samba, plus goals from Rayan Cherki, Allan, and Ryan McAidoo, sealed Manchester City's victory. Enzo Maresca's side will now face Brighton in the fourth-round of the competition after they swept aside Norwich City tonight.

Enzo Maresca used tonight's third-round Carabao Cup tie as an opportunity to rotate his squad. Maresca made 10 changes from the starting eleven which beat Manchester United at Old Trafford. Gerónimo Rulli, Floyd Samba and Allan all made their debuts for Manchester City, which was a special moment for each player.

Manchester City began the game brightly. Enzo Maresca's side were patient and composed in possession to begin the match. Norwich City were looking to be tight and compact in defence and hit on the break when the opportunity arose. Rico Lewis fired the first significant shot of the game over the crossbar in the 9th minute. Abdukodir Khusanov played a ball to Floyd Samba in midfield, and Samba's neat flick set Lewis clean through on goal. However, Lewis fired a great chance over the crossbar and Norwich City keeper Daniel Grimshaw was happy to see Lewis' shot fly harmlessly behind for a goal kick.

As the game ticked into the 20th minute, there was a laboured feel to proceedings. Enzo Maresca's side were dominating possession without creating any real openings. Norwich City were defending resolutely and did look to carry a threat on the rare occasions that they did get forward. Papa Diallo on the left wing in particular did look to be an outlet for Norwich City with his pace and power.

Manchester City took the lead in the 29th minute. Nico O'Reilly was played into space on the left and the England international floated a cross to the back post. Norwich keeper Daniel Grimshaw got a hand to the ball but he only succeeded in palming the ball to Allan. Allan played a first-time cross back into a dangerous area. Floyd Samba scored a diving header on target that beat Daniel Grimshaw to give City a 1-0 lead. It was a clever finish by Floyd Samba and the young attacking midfielder had his first goal on first team debut for Manchester City. It was a fantastic moment for Samba, which he thoroughly enjoyed.

Enzo Maresca's side doubled their lead three minutes later. City played through midfield and Ayyoub Bouaddi received a nice first-time ball from Floyd Samba before playing a quality through ball to Rayan Cherki, who was in behind the Norwich City defence after finding acres of space on the left. Cherki raced clear and beat the oncoming Daniel Grimshaw with a composed right-footed finish from just outside the penalty area to double City's lead.

Floyd Samba would curl an effort over the crossbar in the 37th minute. Samba was picked out by Ayyoub Bouaddi just inside the Norwich City penalty area. Samba, filled with confidence from his early goal and overall display, attempted to curl an effort into the top corner from just inside the penalty area. However, his effort went high and wide. What was prominent, as it was for Rayan Cherki's goal, was when Ayyoub Bouaddi had space to pick out a pass he was unlocking the Norwich City defence with ease.

Outside of a Rayan Ait-Nouri shot that was fired over the bar, the remainder of the first half played out without incident. Manchester City would take a well-deserved 2-0 lead into the interval. Enzo Maresca's side had dominated possession and were good value for their lead.

Manchester City barely raised a sweat during the first half. It took time for a new-look City lineup to click into gear. But when they did, Norwich City didn't have an answer. The performances of Floyd Samba and Ayyoub Bouaddi were superb. Samba was lively up front and his goal was a special moment and well-deserved for his efforts. Bouaddi was a cut above and when he had space to pick out an incisive pass his impact was tremendous. Rayan Cherki was also a cut above throughout the first half and his goal, plus his tricks and flicks were entertaining as always.

Ryan McAidoo replaced Rayan Cherki at halftime as Enzo Maresca looked to be saving Cherki for Sunday's Premier League fixture against Sunderland. Ryan McAidoo slotted in on the right wing with Allan moving to the left wing. Rayan Ait-Nouri moved to left-back with Nico O'Reilly slotting into midfield as the number ten.

Manchester City took a 3-0 lead in the 48th minute. Allan received possession from Rayan Ait-Nouri on the left wing. The Brazilian winger drove at Norwich City defender Sam Field, who was stranded on an island against Allan. Allan's dribbling forced Field into his own area before the Brazilian winger dropped his shoulder to the left which was a great piece of skill and beat Daniel Grimshaw with a quality low finish. The goal was absolutely brilliant and provided a glimpse of what Allan can do.

Norwich City would play themselves into trouble trying to play out from the back in the 54th minute. Daniel Grimshaw played a poor ball to his teammate on the edge of his own area who attempted to play a ball out to the right-back. Rayan Ait-Nouri nicked in to seize possession in a dangerous position. Initially, Ait-Nouri slipped and it seemed that the chance was gone. However, Rayan Ait-Nouri regained his feet and played the ball back to Floyd Samba. Samba curled a low effort across Daniel Grimshaw from the left to bag himself a brace in a dream debut for the young attacking midfielder.

For Norwich City, substitute Anthony Musaba fired a volley inches wide in the 63rd minute. The visitors had a corner from the right that was cleared to the edge of the penalty area by the Manchester City defence. Musaba took a touch before hitting a sweet left-footed volley on goal which drifted just wide with Gerónimo Rulli at full stretch to try and make a save. Musaba's effort went inches wide and would have been a spectacular goal if it had gone in.

Ryan McAidoo almost got himself on the scoresheet in the 69th minute. Floyd Samba received possession up front and he played a neat ball to Ryan McAidoo in space on the right. McAidoo got a right-footed shot in on goal that Norwich City keeper Daniel Grimshaw got down well to save to his right.

Norwich City would have the ball in the back of the net in the 75th minute. Anthony Musaba slipped Mo Toure in behind the City defence and the Australian striker beat the oncoming Gerónimo Rulli with a composed low finish. However, Toure had stayed offside and the goal was ruled out. The organisation between Vitor Reis and Abdukodir Khusanov was good to see to trap the Australian striker offside.

Manchester City would make it 5-0 in the 90th minute. Nico O'Reilly was played into space on the left behind the Norwich City defence. O'Reilly squared the ball across where Floyd Samba let the ball run with a clever dummy before Ryan McAidoo beat Daniel Grimshaw with a quality finish on the right to cap off a fantastic night for Enzo Maresca's side and the Manchester City academy.

McAidoo's goal would be the final moment of the match as Manchester City booked themselves a fourth-round tie against Brighton at the Etihad Stadium.

Manchester City began their defence of the Carabao Cup with an emphatic 5-0 win. Enzo Maresca's side were rarely troubled on the night and it took them 20 minutes to get going but once they did, they swept Norwich City aside.

Floyd Samba was the star of the show as he bagged a brace in his Manchester City first-team debut. Allan showed glimpses of what he'll add to Enzo Maresca's side as he grabbed a goal and an assist in his City debut. More impressively, every City player on the pitch showed something which illustrated the options at Enzo Maresca's disposal this season.

title: Patrick Queen voices support for Joey Porter Jr
description: Steelers LB Patrick Queen shows support for Joey Porter Jr.
fullText:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. left the media viewing portion of practice early on Thursday. Porter walked off the field with a Steelers trainer after only a few individual workouts. The reasoning for Porter Jr.'s absence is not yet known and head coach Mike McCarthy said before practice that Porter Jr. was scheduled to do more work today than in yesterday's practice.

Porter Jr. was listed as a limited participant, but his designation was changed from a back injury to non-injury related/conditioning. This stems from Porter Jr. being in the PUP list for all of training camp in Latrobe with a lingering back issue, but the cloud of a potential contract extension over his head. He did not play in the season opener against Atlanta and may not play in New England this Sunday.

Linebacker Patrick Queen backed Porter Jr., regardless of whether the contract or injury is the main reason why he hasn't played or fully practiced.

"Joey, whatever he's going through, whether it's injury or contract, I respect it," Queen said on Thursday, per Chris Adamski of The Trib.

The Steelers are the only team in the NFL that have a policy against negotiating during the season.

"I'm behind him 100%," Queen said. "I tell him every single time, 'I respect how you go about your business every single day. I know you all see the stuff he does out there. I definitely respect him."

Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamel Dean limited the Falcons to 143 yards passing, albeit with backup Cooper Rush at quarterback. The defense did its job against Atlanta, but could soon significantly miss Porter Jr. if he isn't back for the Bengals next Sunday.

Steelers players have publicly backed Porter Jr. during this saga, including Jalen Ramsey who emphatically told the media the Steelers should pay Porter Jr. before the season.

Let us know what you think in the comments. Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

title: Jürgen Klopp praises former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann
description: The current Germany boss acknowledged his predecessor and his qualities
fullText:
Julian Nagelsmann was manager of the German national football team for almost three years, and his tenure was not the kind that Germany fans hoped for from the former Bayern Munich manager. Nagelsmann's replacement, Jürgen Klopp, spoke more positively about him.

"I've been doing this job for 25 years; Julian Nagelsmann was 13 back then. I have immense respect for him," Klopp said in a recent press conference (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia). "I had a lot of trouble playing against his Hoffenheim side with Liverpool. He's an exceptional coach, 100%." Klopp's Liverpool played Nagelsmann's Hoffenheim side in the Champions League playoffs in the 2017/18 season; Liverpool won 6-3 on aggregate.

Nagelsmann was seen as one of the brightest young coaches in Europe, performing miracles with a modest Hoffenheim side which earned him a move to RB Leipzig, Bayern and then the German national team. Although his stock has since slumped due to subpar performances with Die Mannschaft, he is only 39-years-old and he still has enough time to prove why he used to be one of the most promising tacticians around.

title: End of Season Minor League News Roundup
description: The Jays are in the thick of a slapstick caper of a wildcard race, but with today being an off day I thought I’d look at the minor leagues as their seasons wrap up. The International League (AAA) goes through this weekend, so the Buffalo Bisons have a few more to play, but the other […]
fullText:
The Jays are in the thick of a slapstick caper of a wildcard race, but with today being an off day I thought I'd look at the minor leagues as their seasons wrap up. The International League (AAA) goes through this weekend, so the Buffalo Bisons have a few more to play, but the other levels' seasons came to a close over the course of the last couple of weeks.

The Vancouver Canadians won the Northwest League championship in a 12 inning thriller on Friday night. You can read a full recap here, but it involved a three run comeback in the ninth to force extras and plenty of other drama. It's the Canadians' sixth league championship since they became a Blue Jays affiliate in 2011, and their second since the Northwest League was converted from short season ball to A+ in the minor league reorganization.

As Tom mentioned in his roundup yesterday, the rosters for the Arizona Fall League were released. The AFL is a developmental league that is mostly used to give prospects who missed time or otherwise need a little more work an opportunity for some additional reps. This year, it runs from October 3rd through November 14th. Because the number of players teams want to send is limited, especially on the pitching side, AFL rosters are blended. The Jays team up with the Cubs, A's, Red Sox and Angels to form the Mesa Solar Sox.

Participation in the AFL can be a big opportunity for prospects. They get a chance to shine when there aren't any other minor leagues going, with scouts from all 30 teams paying attention. Recent proof is Spencer Miles, who caught the Jays' attention with 8.2 impressive innings in last year's AFL.

The Jays prospects going this year are:

Brandon Barriera: The 2022 first round pick has alternated between injured and ineffective so far in his career. This season was more of the same, as he managed just 38.2 innings but walked 29 in that span. He's managed just 66 innings over four pro seasons, so the Jays are likely both inclined to get him more action and not too concerned with sheltering him anymore.

Gilberto Batista: It was a rough year for Batista. He recorded a 7.86 ERA across 87 innings as a multi-inning reliever for Vancouver. He did show some promise last year with Dunedin, after being acquired from the Red Sox in the Danny Jansen trade.

Jake Bloss: Bloss is the exciting name from a Jays fan point of view. He came back from Tommy John surgery throwing 2mph harder than he had before the surgery, but then went down almost immediately with a teres major strain. If he can make a few healthy appearances, retain the stuff bump, and continue to rediscover his command after the surgery, he'll be set up for a potential rotation role with the big league club next year.

Fernando Perez: The word for Perez' season is mysterious. He ranked high on our prospect list last winter on the strength of his elite command and strong results across A+ Vancouver and AA New Hampshire, but had a disastrous start to his 2026, walking 10 in nine innings over his first three starts. He was placed on the Development List, a new addition to the minors since the 2021 reorganization that basically allows teams to take players off the roster indefinitely to manage workloads or to work on things outside of game action. He returned for three more appearances in August and September and didn't look any better. Command is Perez' whole draw as a prospect, so losing it so completely is concerning. The AFL will be a big opportunity to show that he's righted the ship. He's Rule 5 eligible, and coming into the season I'd have expected him to warrant protection, but that seems a distant concern now.

Yondrei Rojas: Our #32 prospect entering the season, Rojas struggled to build on his strong 2025 this year. He struck out just 20% of batters, mostly at AA, and missed fewer bats that last season. He's 23 and Rule 5 eligible, so this might be one more chance to harness his plus fastball-slider combination and mark himself as a future Blue Jays bullpen hand.

Aaron Parker: 2026 was a breakout for the third year pro. He cut down his swing rate and went on a power binge at New Hampshire, launching 19 home runs in 87 games. He's a below average defensive catcher and his 67% contact rate is scary, but plus power is plus power, and he may have a shot at the third catcher role at some point in 2027.

Jake Casey: The Kent State prospect has just hit since the Jays took him in the 15th round last year. This season, a broken hamate wiped out his first couple of months, but he managed 13 home runs in just 64 games. He still needs to show he can adjust to upper minors quality spin, and the results are iffy so far, but as long as he keeps producing he'll warrant watching.

Jake Cook: Last year's third rounder was just average in A ball, which would be concerning for most pedigreed college draftees. Cook is just two years into switching back to the field from the mound, though, and working to overhaul the pure slap, inside-out swing he used in college to try to develop a modicum of power. He did up his home run total over last year, from 3 to 5, in spite of switching to wood bats and facing better pitching, and he improved as the year went on. He was also 22 for 27 stealing bases, showcasing the athletic tools that convinced the Jays to gamble a top 100 pick on him. He needs reps, and the AFL will offer an opportunity against pitching a bit better than he's seen so far.

Because they share a team with the Angels, the Jay's prospects will get a chance to catch up with Arjun Nimmala. He finished the season red hot, clubbing four home runs and four doubles last week for the AA Rocket City Trash Pandas.

Baseball America has graded the year for each farm system. They give the Jays a B+ overall, which seems about right to me. When I reviewed the performance of the top 40 before the deadline, there were a lot of guys moving in different directions, but the overall trend seemed to be upwards.

There were several impressive breakouts, although many of those guys will miss next year's list because they've already graduated. Miles, Brandon Valenzuela, and Brett Bateman have all already far exceeded their prospect expectations. Valenzuela has fallen off badly in the second half and Bateman is surely playing over his head offensively, but both still project as at least quality role players now. For Miles, his peripheral stats fully support his exceptional performance this year, and continued health seems like the only real question. Still on the farm is Nolan Perry, who returned from Tommy John and immediately torched three levels, striking out 117 in only 82.2 innings. Sean Keys, who raced through AA and AAA early in the season, is in between. He's with the Jays right now but not seeing a lot of playing time. His early MLB results haven't been good, but the underlying contact and power data remain tantalizing.

Of course, there were some disappointments as well. Bloss showcased improved stuff in his own TJ comeback, but remained healthy only briefly. Juan Sanchez, last year's Dominican Summer League star, has so far failed to consistently translate his success in the US. Ricky Tiedemann, among others, continued to struggle with his health.

The farm's ranking, in BA's reckoning, rose from 17 to 15 between the preseason and the midseason update. That's impressive given that a lot of the preseason value was tied to Trey Yesavage, who graduated soon after returning from his early season shoulder issues. They might dip slightly this winter, as they traded top prospect Arjun Nimmala and had fewer resources in the draft than most other teams, but the system produced new talent, fed the major league team, and allowed them to make major deadline acquisitions without moving backwards in overall talent. That's a good year.

title: Europa League: After blasting De Zerbi, ex scores v Marseille 💥
description: He can believe in his karma.This Thursday evening, OM are in serious trouble, trailing 3-1 away to Beşiktaş on matchday one of the Europa League.The third goal of the match is all the more cruel for...
fullText:
This Thursday evening, OM are in serious trouble, trailing 3-1 away to Beşiktaş on matchday one of the Europa League.

The third goal of the match is all the more cruel for the Olympians as it was scored by a former club player, Amir Murillo.

Forced out of the club during the previous winter transfer window after a falling-out with Roberto De Zerbi, the Panamanian defender had not been kind to the club before the match.

"I think everyone understood that I had a problem with the coach, not with the team or the club. It was personal; in a way, I felt he had disrespected me. They practically forced me to leave the club, and that's how I ended up at Beşiktaş," he had explained.

It should be noted that tonight, Medhi Benatia responded to him on Canal+, also not hesitating to be sharp.

"It's a little easy to come out with that now, when everyone has moved on. Amir, I remember what he said, it helped him play at this level. I remember when he arrived from Anderlecht, he was a substitute. He has always been hardworking, he's a very good lad. We were a bit bothered by the situation," said the former OM sporting director.

Be that as it may, Marseille are currently two goals behind and will have to dig deep to get back level.

title: What to know about the giant bison outside the Bills' new stadium
description: The massive bison greeting fans at the new Highmark Stadium have a story. Here's why they're there and how big they are.
fullText:
As Buffalo Bills fans stream into the new Highmark Stadium for the first regular-season game in its history Thursday night, they'll be greeted by a family of towering bison statues standing watch outside the stadium.

The sculptures, installed this summer, have quickly become one of the defining visual elements of the Bills' new home.

Here's how the larger-than-life statues came together, what they symbolize and why they became such a prominent part of the stadium's design.

Created by artist Blessing Hancock, the statues are built around a steel frame with a stainless steel exterior. The installation is designed to represent the strength, resilience and family spirit of Buffalo and Bills Mafia.

The display includes a bull, cow and calf, a family grouping that was intentionally chosen to symbolize togetherness and generations of Bills Mafia fans.

The statues were fabricated by ART Research Enterprises in Lancaster, Pennsylvania.

The bull stands approximately 27 feet tall, stretches 29 feet long and weighs about 23,000 pounds. The cow stands about 22 feet tall and 23 feet long, while the calf measures roughly 12 feet tall and 13 feet long. The sculptures feature programmable lighting, and the bull and cow can emit vapor from their nostrils to create the appearance of breathing on a cold Western New York night.

The Family Circle is a year-round gathering space outside the stadium's secure entrance. The plaza also features the Bills Legend Wall honoring members of the franchise's Wall of Fame and displays celebrating western New York history.

The organization officially opened the new $2.2 billion Highmark Stadium with a ribbon-cutting ceremony in June.

Although the sculptures were installed this summer, Thursday's opener marks the first time they'll welcome a full regular-season crowd.

This article originally appeared on Rochester Democrat and Chronicle: What to know about the giant bison outside the Bills' new stadium
